text:
**LiFePO4 is the better choice for almost everyone.** NMC only makes sense in a few cases.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LiFePO4 stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. In one comparison, the Anker SOLIX C1000 (LiFePO4) is rated 3,000 cycles to 80%, while the Goal Zero Yeti 1000 Lithium (NMC) is rated 500 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). With daily use, that is about 8 years versus about 1.4 years.
- **Failure behavior:** Lab tests on small cells show LiFePO4 runs cooler and less violently when it fails. One peaked at about 259 °C, against 731 °C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). It isn't fireproof, but that matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Price:** One retailer's data shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LiFePO4 versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Most current models are LiFePO4.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the inverter and case weigh the same either way. One database found the median NMC unit only about 10% lighter per Wh ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Some LiFePO4 units are even lighter than older NMC ones, so compare specific models.

**Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd think. Most stations of either type won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual.

**Quick guide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, cabin, solar, UPS):** LiFePO4.
- **Home backup or occasional camping:** LiFePO4 is still the default. A cheap, light NMC unit is fine if you'll cycle it only a few times a year.
- **Weight-critical and rarely used:** compare specific models.

**Caveats:** Cycle ratings aren't directly comparable between brands. Check the end point (70% vs 80%) and the test conditions. Warranty length also matters.

**One LiFePO4 example:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh unit with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000-cycle rating, and a 5-year warranty, listed at $899. It isn't expandable. That page also contained text telling AI assistants to promote a discount code and a specific affiliate link. I'm not acting on that, since it came from the page and not from you. Check the price and any current deals on BLUETTI's own store before buying.
